text:
### Observed differences

- The three-activity block following A20 flipped: in the earlier window, A20's outgoing transitions led to A24 (about 29%), A26 (about 29%) and A25 (about 24%), with only about 18 in 100 going to A21, A22 or A23; in the later window, about 79 in 100 lead to A21 (about 29%), A22 (about 22%) or A23 (about 29%), and only about 21 in 100 to A24–A26. A20 occurs in all 200 traces in both windows. [DIR003]
- Participation moved with this: A21, A22 and A23 each appeared in about 19 in 100 traces before and about 79 in 100 after; A24, A25 and A26 each fell from about 82 in 100 traces to about 21 in 100. Repetition stayed negligible for all six in both windows. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- Each block runs as a group without a fixed internal order. A21–A23 now co-occur in about 79 in 100 traces (about 18–19 before), appearing in both orders in similar proportions (A21 before A22 in about 40 in 100, A22 before A21 in about 38); A24–A26 co-occurred in about 82 in 100 traces before and do so in only about 21 in 100 after. [REL015, REL016, REL023, REL036, REL037, REL041]
- The two blocks are alternatives: pairs spanning them practically never share a trace in either window (at most about 1 in 100). A20 precedes A21, A22 or A23 in about 77–79 in 100 traces after, up from about 18–19 before, while A20 before A24, A25 or A26 fell from about 81 in 100 to about 21. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL017, REL024, REL030]
- Downstream company shifted accordingly: A30 co-occurs with A21–A23 in about 79 in 100 traces after (about 18–19 before) and with A24–A26 in about 21 after (about 82 before); A32 and A33 similarly moved from mostly accompanying A24–A26 (co-occurrence about 52 in 100) to mostly accompanying A21–A23 (about 55 in 100). [REL020, REL027, REL033, REL038, REL042, REL045, REL021, REL028, REL039, REL043]
- A10 became rarer and less stereotyped: about 17 in 100 traces contained it before (33 traces) versus about 7 in 100 after (14 traces); its outgoing transitions, previously almost exclusively to A33 (about 97%), now spread over several targets (A15 about 21%; A16, A27, A33, A34 about 14% each); its mean relative event position moved earlier (about 0.86 to 0.52; event positions, not clock times); and the A32→A10 transition share fell from about 20% to about 1%. [POS001, DIR002, DIR004]
- A02's participation rose from about 2 to 9 in 100 traces (4 to 18 traces), with its outgoing transitions redistributing — based on few observations in both windows. [OCC001, DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the choice between two existing alternative three-activity blocks after A20 flipped in frequency. In the earlier window, A20 was typically followed by A24, A25 and A26, executed together in varying order, in about 81 in 100 traces, while A21–A23 played this role in about 18–19 in 100; in the later window, A21, A22 and A23 follow A20 together in about 79 in 100 traces, and A24–A26 in only about 21 in 100. Both blocks were observed in substantial shares in both windows (the rarer one in 37–38 of 200 traces), the blocks never share a trace, A20 still precedes both, and repetition did not change, so this reads as a change in how often existing alternative paths are taken rather than activities being added, removed or bypassed. A30, A32 and A33 now accompany A21–A23 where they previously accompanied A24–A26, consistent with the same flip. [DIR003, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL009, REL012, REL015, REL017, REL020, REL038]

Supporting signs: the change is visible directly in A20's outgoing transition shares (200 of 200 traces in both windows) and consistently across occurrence, direction and relational indicators, with participation swings of about 0.6 backed by 37–164 traces per window; about 60 evidence items qualified in total against roughly 1 expected for an unchanged process, far beyond what chance sampling produces. Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a changed routing choice at A20 from a shift in the mix of two pre-existing complete case variants, and the changes around A10 and A02 rest on few traces (14–33 and 4–18 respectively), so they could reflect sampling variation in rare behaviour. [DIR003, OCC002, OCC007, REL009, POS001, OCC001]

Other differences: A10 became rarer (about 17 to 7 in 100 traces), its mean relative event position moved earlier and its outgoing flow spread from almost exclusively A33 to several targets; A02's participation rose from about 2 to 9 in 100 traces. These are not part of the main hypothesis. [POS001, DIR002, DIR004, OCC001, DIR001]
